question: Does accounting for incomplete personal preferences improve constrained slate choice over point scoring and simple diversity reranking?
stage: development baselines; no new mechanism claimed
sample_rule: lowest sha256(slate-choice-sample-v1:USER_ID), independently per split, after non-value-based activity eligibility
primary_development_metric: paired recall@5 of observed future positives over all sampled dev users; users with none score zero and are separately counted
limitations: retrospective active-user sampling; not population-random request sampling
observed future positives are incomplete relevance judgments, not full user utility
bootstrap predictions are not calibrated user preference posteriors
greedy minimax regret is an approximation, not a certified game equilibrium
genre/year metadata are a static snapshot with year restriction, not verified historical catalog availability
personal rating visibility varies but all past seen item IDs remain available to all methods
reserved_test labels must not be evaluated during development
